Later resolutions can add costs and outputs, so a revised report needs a new cutoff and updated accounting. Discovering a split violation late explains lost usable output; it does not prove that earlier partitioning would have preserved the same task mix, costs, or acceptance yield.

:::

The manifest now states what was emitted, why it is eligible, which targets it carries, and what the collection spent to obtain it. The remaining test of its learning value is a controlled comparison of the resulting policy under the protected evaluation protocol. A cheaper artifact or a higher collection yield cannot substitute for that evidence. The following pitfalls expose ways to lose these distinctions even when every individual processing stage appears to work.

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-vol3-trajectory-curation-fallacies}

A collection pipeline can preserve every record and still produce the wrong learning artifact. The following mistakes confuse evidence about a run with a decision about what a learner should practice.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *A successful task makes every action in its trace a suitable demonstration.*

Task acceptance concerns declared outcomes and constraints. A learning-use decision also considers the behavior to teach, the conditioning information, and the role of each recorded segment. An accepted repair may contain a corrected malformed proposal that should remain visible as context without becoming a desired target. Conversely, a failed run can contain useful decisions or supply a diagnostic fixture. Record validity, final acceptance, and target eligibility are separate judgments.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Improving cascade yield by changing the criteria being compared.*

A cheaper pipeline is not an equivalent alternative if it skips a mandatory predicate or silently discards unresolved cases. Compare the same learning-use conditions, preserve prerequisite and execution-safety constraints, and measure costs under each ordering. Conditional survival rates can change when stages move. Report usable artifacts and pending decisions separately; a high or low yield alone does not establish that the grader is sound.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *A fixed recovery percentage guarantees a resilient policy.*

Trajectory counts, stored tokens, and loss-bearing tokens describe different allocations. Recovery records may be longer, and not every stored segment is selected for imitation. Their value depends on the target tasks, allowed responses, and learning objective. Compare proposed mixtures under a declared training budget and held-out protocol. Recovery can mean a justified hold or escalation rather than autonomous repair, and no mixture removes the need for runtime enforcement.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Treating redaction and deduplication as proof that a corpus is safe and independent.*

A transformation can change meaning or invalidate the evidence for a later action even when the record still parses. Preserve source-to-derived lineage, revalidate the properties needed for its intended use, and hold records with unresolved permissions or sensitive content. Deduplication screens similarity; it does not establish a generalization claim. Related attempts and transformed variants retain their protected split assignment, while optional repository or schema holdouts test separately declared transfer questions.
:::

## Summary {#sec-vol3-trajectory-curation-summary}
[]{#sec-vol3-flywheel-summary}

A log records an attempted task; a curated artifact states how evidence from that attempt may be used for learning. The chapter began with the proposed behavior change, rather than assuming that every evaluated failure required new weights. It then specified collection fixtures and protected evaluation boundaries, applied learning-use admission predicates, and selected coverage across ordinary decisions, errors, and recovery. In the hypothetical collection run producing `ws_r20`, the refused malformed proposal remains history while the assessed correction can become a target. Those choices determine what the collection system must produce and what its output means.

Collection capacity and provenance make that decision operational. Bounded admission accounts for work still in flight as well as completed buffers. Versioned records retain the origin, checks, permissions, transformations, and split assignment needed to inspect a corpus. Cost per emitted artifact includes the unsuccessful and unselected work needed to obtain it. Self-improvement changes the source distribution and selection pressure, so a growing corpus still needs external assessment. The resulting manifest distinguishes demonstrations or selected target-bearing segments, justified comparisons, and fixtures for fresh reward-scored rollouts; it does not treat them as interchangeable training inputs.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Give every learning artifact a declared use"}

* **Justify a learning use before collecting its targets**: Try context, tool and schema, and runtime repairs before weights, guided by counterfactual probes, and train only on the residual failure that survives them. Distinguish demonstrations, context-compatible preference comparisons, and fixtures for fresh reward-scored rollouts; a recorded outcome does not select its own downstream objective.
* **Build fixtures and splits around the claim**: Declare collection conditions, criterion coverage, permitted variation, and known adequate and inadequate controls. Group related attempts before selection and protect held-out answers and evidence. Familiar tools or repositories are not automatically leakage; additional holdouts answer stated transfer questions.
* **Compare admission costs without weakening admission**: Define each predicate, its evidence, and its routing consequence. Preserve mandatory conditions and safe execution prerequisites when changing order, and use the appropriate conditional costs and survival rates. Mechanical checks and calibrated judgments remain limited by their coverage.
* **Separate recorded behavior from selected supervision**: Keep faithful recovery context without endorsing an erroneous action as a target. Negative records can support several declared uses. Report trajectory counts, stored-token shares, and loss-bearing allocation separately, and test mixtures rather than memorizing an allegedly optimal ratio.
* **Evaluate the selection loop as it changes**: A new sampling policy or admission rule can alter which tasks and strategies enter the corpus. Track source versions, coverage, diversity, and relevant staleness, with external assessment kept separate from tuning. More selected successes alone do not establish broader improvement.
* **Bound collection work before buffers fill**: Relate admitted work to downstream service and storage capacity, accounting for active rollouts, queued records, bytes, and reservations. Average utilization does not guarantee a delay bound. Backpressure limits new admission without erasing unfinished operations or their cleanup and accounting duties.
* **Make the corpus manifest an inspectable contract**: Bind records and derived artifacts to source versions, checks, transformations, applicable permissions, split membership, and intended consumers. Integrity does not establish truth or permission. Revalidate modified material and preserve unresolved decisions instead of silently inheriting approval from the original bytes.

:::

Verified trajectory post-training (principle \ref{pri-vol3-trajectory-post-training}) now has a concrete decision boundary: evidence supports a specified learning use, not automatic imitation of a successful log. The corpus manifest preserves that decision through selection and transformation so the trainer can distinguish context from intended targets. Any resulting policy change still requires evaluation and remains subject to the runtime's authority and resource controls.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From corpus membership to learning targets"}

Which tokens should a model be trained to produce from these admitted records? @Sec-vol3-fine-tuning turns the curation contract into serialized examples and objectives. It must preserve the intended conditioning context, construct the selected token-level targets, and keep independent examples from acquiring unintended information through batching. Preference learning applies a different objective to justified comparisons. Curation determines which material is eligible and why; the next chapter determines how that material contributes to an update and how the changed policy is evaluated.

:::
